synonimy: Des-(6-39)-human blood-coagulation factor X light chain (98-108')- disulfide with (185'-alanine (S>a))human activated factor xa heavy chain, produced in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells (glycoform alfa)
sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

Coagulation factor Xa (andexanet alfa) has been removed from the market in the United States because of the clotting risk. No information is available on the clinical use of coagulation factor Xa during breastfeeding. Because it is a large protein molecule with a molecular weight of about 40,000 Da, the amount in milk is likely to be very low and absorption is unlikely because it is probably destroyed in the infant's gastrointestinal tract. Until more data become available, coagulation factor X should be used with caution during breastfeeding, especially while nursing a newborn or preterm infant.
